name: Finnish Karjalanpiirakka
description: Karjalanpiirakka, Finnish Karelian pies, are genuinely built on a paper-thin rye crust pinched from both sides toward the center in small folds, leaving the rice porridge filling visible - real technique cooks the rice slowly in milk for a full 45 minutes into a genuine porridge, not just plain boiled rice, and the hot pies are always finished with munavoi, chopped egg worked into softened butter, spread on right before eating.
steps_detailed: Simmer the rice with the milk over low heat, stirring occasionally, 40-45 minutes, until it becomes a thick, cohesive porridge. Let cool.
Mix the rye and all-purpose flour with enough water to form a firm dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Roll the dough paper-thin and cut into ovals.
Spread the rice porridge in the center of each oval, then pinch the edges from both sides toward the center in small folds, leaving the filling visible.
Brush lightly with butter and bake at 450F (230C) for 12-15 minutes until the edges are golden.
Chop the hard-boiled egg and mash it into the remaining softened butter to make munavoi, and spread it on the pies while still hot.

name: Finnish Lohikeitto
description: Lohikeitto, a real creamy salmon soup, is a beloved Finnish comfort dish, real technique adding fresh dill at the very end so its flavor stays bright rather than cooking away.
steps_detailed: Simmer the potato and leeks in 2 cups water 15-18 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the salmon and cream, and simmer 8-10 minutes until the salmon is just cooked through.
Stir in the fresh dill right at the end, off the heat, so its flavor stays bright.

name: Finnish Pulla
description: Pulla, cardamom-spiced sweet bread, is a beloved Finnish coffee-break staple, real technique using a genuinely generous amount of real cardamom, which is what defines pulla's distinctive aroma.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, cardamom (being generous, since this is what defines pulla), sugar, softened butter, egg, and baking powder with a little milk into a soft dough.
Shape into a small braided loaf or rolls.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 18-20 minutes until golden.

name: Finnish Ruisleipä (Rye Bread)
description: Ruisleipä, dense dark rye bread, is Finland's most essential daily staple, real rye flour used directly here for its genuine dense, earthy character.
steps_detailed: Mix the rye flour, baking powder, and honey with enough water to form a firm, dense dough.
Shape into a small round loaf and bake at 375F (190C) for 30-35 minutes until firm.

name: Finnish Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad with real dill, a common Finnish side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar and sugar together, toss with the cucumber and dill.
